name: Wildlife Diversity Grant Program (2027-2029)

funder.name: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

summary: Biennial grants for conservation and recovery actions and data collection for at-risk Washington wildlife, via a pre-proposal and invited full proposal. Habitat restoration, easements and land acquisition are not funded.

eligibility.rule: Applicant is affiliated with an entity that will enter a grant agreement if selected
Project activities benefit species populations in Washington
Project benefits eligible SGCN or SGIN
Project does not primarily involve habitat restoration, conservation easements, or land acquisition
Project is not focused on general outreach or environmental education
Project does not primarily benefit species outside WDFW Wildlife Diversity Division's scope
Non-tribal projects on tribal lands or using tribal data have written tribal permission

calls.label: 2027-2029 biennium pre-proposals
calls.note: Pre-proposal deadline; selected applicants are then invited to submit full proposals

status.quote: Grant applicants must complete a pre-proposal application form no later than 11:59 p.m. on Nov. 13, 2026.

opens.quote: Pre-proposal period and submission form opens Oct. 5, 2026

deadline.quote: Grant applicants must complete a pre-proposal application form no later than 11:59 p.m. on Nov. 13, 2026.

applicant_types.quote: Applicants who are affiliated with public, nonprofit, academic, or tribal entities are eligible to submit proposals.

geography.quote: Proposed projects must take place within Washington

access.quote: Grant applicants must complete a pre-proposal application form no later than 11:59 p.m. on Nov. 13, 2026.

amount.quote: Grant budgets can range from a minimum of $25,000 and a maximum of $250,000 per project.

co_finance_required.quote: Cost sharing or matching is not required, but WDFW may consider this favorably when evaluating proposals.

effort.quote: Grant applicants must submit a pre-proposal application form no later than 11:59 p.m. on Nov. 13, 2026.
The deadline for a full proposal is Jan. 25, 2027.

eligibility.quote: The applicant must be affiliated with a public, nonprofit, academic, or tribal entity that will enter a grant agreement with WDFW should their proposal be selected for funding.
WDFW staff are not eligible to receive funds from this program.
All project activities must be directed toward benefitting species populations in Washington.
Projects that benefit the following SGCN and SGIN are eligible for this grant funding.
Habitat restoration2, conservation easements, or land acquisition
Projects that are focused on general outreach and environmental education are not eligible for this grant opportunity.
Projects that primarily benefit species outside WDFW Wildlife Diversity Division's scope of responsibility are not eligible.
Any proposals by non-tribal entities for projects that include activities on tribal reservation lands, or use of tribal data, must provide written permission from the respective tribe(s).

after_award.quote: Grantees will be expected to provide WDFW progress reports on project activities to date and provide all deliverables for the pay period.
